title: Laredo Overdose Deaths Climb to 10 in October as DEA Builds First-in-the-Nation Prevention Program for Kindergarteners

content:
Overdose deaths in Laredo rose from seven in September to 10 in October, according to police — a jump of more than 40 percent in a single month — and officials are now building a drug prevention program aimed at children as young as 5.

The Drug Enforcement Administration is partnering with Texas A&M to create the program, KGNS reported. It will use cartoons and bilingual lessons to help kindergarteners learn what is safe to touch and what to avoid.

DEA agent Dr. Robert Kennedy said the effort comes after a spike in children being exposed to drugs at home. Kennedy said the program would be the first of its kind in the United States.

“This will be something that's very big because it is not done anywhere in the United States. No one is actually talking to kindergarteners to actually say, hey, this is what you should be doing. This is what you shouldn't touch,” Kennedy said.

Officials said the goal is to reach every neighborhood in Laredo, and they plan to expand the program to include parent education classes starting next year.

The rise in deaths comes just as the city took one of its most visible steps against the drug trade: on Wednesday, Nov. 25, crews demolished a house at Olive Street and Sanders Avenue that Laredo police linked to years of drug activity and at least five overdose deaths since 2023.

Demolishing a house removes a location. The new program tries something different — reaching children before drugs reach them. Whether a cartoon-based curriculum for 5-year-olds can move the numbers in a city where overdose deaths just jumped 40 percent in a month is the question Webb Watch 956 will keep following as the program takes shape.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 26, 2026; Laredo Police Department.
